text:
alex: Heads up — CI perf run on canary flagged a regression after the last release. Observed p99 token latency +18% for the int4+fp8 profile on the 8k-seq workload. Uploading flamegraphs and traces now.

perf-ci-bot: CI run 2026-03-16T14:12Z -> https://ci.internal/runs/4829 (perf check failed, regression detected) :warning:

maya: ugh. any obvious diffs in kernel selection? did the matmul kernels flip or did batching change? :eyes:

liam: quick profile dump (from the canary VM):
```
Top hotspots (wall ms):
- dequant_merge_path: 142.1ms (45%)
- matmul_int4_coarse_kernel_v3: 62.3ms (20%)
- matmul_int8_fast_kernel: 19.6ms (6%)
- memcpy_kv_cache: 34.2ms (11%)
- batch_coalesce_worker: 18.9ms (6%)
KV cache hit_rate: 78% (baseline 92%)
Avg batch size: 3.1 (baseline 6.8)
```
liam: note the kernel switch — we're using matmul_int4_coarse_kernel_v3 instead of the int8_fast path for a lot more requests; dequant is huge now.

sophia: that avg batch size drop + lower KV hit_rate screams batch coalescing tweak. Did we change coalesce thresholds in the scheduler?

alex: I grabbed the last merged PR: 0e3c4b2 — "scheduler: coalesce small batches to reduce GPU kernel churn". The change lowered coalesce_threshold from 8 -> 4 and added a fast-path that flushes batches at 50ms.

alex: snippet from the merge commit:
```
- coalesce_threshold: 8
+ coalesce_threshold: 4
+ flush_timeout_ms: 50
```
alex: That would explain smaller batches and worse KV reuse.

jordan: smaller batches -> shorter seq aggregation -> different kernel heuristics pick the int4 coarse kernel because it has better startup for tiny shapes. But overall throughput suffers because more dequant/memcpy overhead per token.

maya: can someone repro locally with the canary config + 8k-seq loadgen? I can run a bisect but need a deterministic repro.

liam: I ran a local microbench with synthetic traffic and reproduced p99 increase ~+15% when coalesce_threshold=4 vs 8. Repro steps:
```
./scripts/loadgen --profile int4_fp8 --seq 8000 --concurrency 48 --duration 10m --coalesce-threshold 4
# baseline: --coalesce-threshold 8
```
liam: produced same kernel selection and KV hit drop.

sophia: ROI-wise, that coalescing change was aimed at reducing kernel churn for short sequences, but it backfired for long-tail 8k requests. For int4+fp8 we depend on bigger batches to favor int8/int4 fast kernels that amortize dequant.

alex: impact: this is a rollout-blocker for canary deploy. CI flagged it; we shouldn't roll to prod.

maya: agree. plan: 1) bisect CI to confirm exact commit (0e3c4b2 is prime suspect) 2) revert or quick-tune coalesce config for canary 3) run extended perf CI with KV metrics. I'll pick bisect.

jordan: quick mitigation idea — add a model-aware coalesce policy: if avg seq_len > 1024, use coalesce_threshold=8; else 4. Might be a medium-term fix.

liam: for immediate rollback I'll open a minimal revert PR to restore coalesce_threshold=8 and remove flush_timeout. I can get that out in 30m.

alex: thanks. please mark the canary rollout as blocked and notify SRE. I'll add an incident tag. :thumbsup:

perf-ci-bot: updated run status -> blocked_by_regression (canary).

maya: assigning follow-ups: @liam: revert PR + test; @maya: run expanded perf CI and collect KV metrics; @sophia: draft long-term scheduler policy proposal.

liam: on it. I'll include flamegraphs and a small benchmark comparing dequant time before/after.

sophia: FYI, also seeing fp8 path is slightly faster in our environment when batches are large; the combined int4+fp8 heuristic needs to prefer fp8 for seq_len>2048 in current kernels. Will write notes.

alex: good. Keep thread updated. If anyone finds another contributing change (kernel selection heuristics or kernel threshold metadata) post here.

maya: thanks — I'll run the bisect now and report earliest bad commit if it's not 0e3c4b2.

jordan: tl;dr — change in scheduler batching heuristics reduced batch sizes -> changed kernel selection -> dequant + memcpy overheads increased -> p99 regression. Revert or conditional thresholds until smarter policy in place.

alex: filing rollout-blocker ticket: RID-2026. I'll link PRs and CI runs here.

liam: PR #4367 opened: "revert: scheduler coalesce threshold change" -> https://git.internal/pr/4367

perf-ci-bot: PR build triggered -> https://ci.internal/pr/4367 (perf tests queued)

maya: running extended perf CI now. will post numbers once it's done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
